title_en: Organic Law of Village Committees of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purpose of improving the system of primary-level self-governance by the masses, enabling villagers to handle their own affairs according to law, developing democracy at the primary level, safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of villagers, promoting the comprehensive revitalization of rural areas, and modernizing the governance system and governance capacity at the primary level.

A villagers committee is a primary-level mass self-governance organization in which villagers practice self-management, self-service, self-education, and self-supervision, and shall practice democratic elections, democratic consultations, democratic decision-making, democratic management, and democratic supervision.
The villagers committee shall handle the public affairs and public welfare undertakings of the village, mediate civil disputes, assist in maintaining public security, reflect villagers' opinions and demands to the people's government, and make suggestions.
The villagers committee shall be responsible for and report on its work to the villagers assembly and the villagers representative assembly.

A villagers committee shall be established based on the living conditions of the villagers, the size of the population, and in accordance with the principles of facilitating villagers' self-governance and being conducive to economic development and primary-level governance.
The establishment, dissolution, or scope adjustment of a villagers committee shall be proposed by the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town, discussed and approved by the villagers assembly, and reported to the people's government at the county level for approval.
A villagers committee may, based on factors such as the living conditions of the villagers and the ownership of collective land, establish several villagers groups.

The work of the villagers committee shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, uphold and develop whole-process people's democracy, and integrate self-governance, rule of law, and rule of virtue.
The grassroots organizations of the Communist Party of China in rural areas shall carry out their work in accordance with the Constitution of the Communist Party of China, lead and support the villagers committee in exercising its functions and powers; and, in accordance with the Constitution and laws, support and guarantee that villagers carry out self-governance activities and directly exercise democratic rights.

The central and local departments for guidance and supervision of primary-level mass self-governance shall be responsible for guiding and supervising the work of rural primary-level mass self-governance.

The people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town shall provide guidance, support, and assistance to the work of the villagers committee, but shall not interfere with matters that fall within the scope of villagers' self-governance according to law.
The villagers committee shall assist the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town in carrying out its work.

Organizations and individuals that have made outstanding contributions to the work of villagers' self-governance shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

A villagers committee shall be composed of three to seven members, including a director, deputy directors, and members.
Among the members of the villagers committee, there shall be female members. Members of the villagers committee shall practice avoidance of close relatives.
The director of the villagers committee may be concurrently held by the head of the village Party organization through statutory procedures. Members of the villagers committee and members of the leading body of the village Party organization may hold concurrent posts.

A villagers committee may, as needed, set up committees for people's mediation, public security, public health, human settlement environment, work concerning the elderly, women, and children, among others. Members of the villagers committee may concurrently serve as members of the subordinate committees. In a village with a small population, the villagers committee may not set up subordinate committees, and its members shall be responsible for the relevant work through division of duties.

The villagers committee shall support and organize villagers to develop various forms of cooperative economy and other economies according to law, undertake the service and coordination work for the production of the village, and promote rural production construction and economic development.
In accordance with the provisions of laws, the villagers committee shall guide villagers to rationally utilize natural resources, protect and improve the ecological environment, and promote the construction of beautiful villages.
The villagers committee shall respect and support the autonomy of rural collective economic organizations to independently carry out economic activities according to law, uphold the two-tier management system based on household contract management with the combination of unified and separate management, and protect the property rights and other legitimate rights and interests of rural collective economic organizations and villagers, contracted households, joint households or partnerships. Where no rural collective economic organization is established, the villagers committee or the villagers group may, according to law, exercise the functions of a rural collective economic organization on its behalf.

The villagers committee shall publicize the Constitution, laws, and regulations, publicize the policies of the Party and the State, support and facilitate villagers to fulfill the obligations prescribed by laws, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of villagers, support and guide villagers to practice the core socialist values, forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, develop culture and education, popularize scientific and technological knowledge, promote gender equality and family harmony, care for the elderly, left-behind children, disabled persons, and villagers in difficulty, enhance solidarity and mutual assistance, promote the transformation of outdated customs, and cultivate civilized rural customs.
The villagers committee shall assist in organizing villagers to participate in mass prevention and mass governance, assist in handling petition matters and mediating and resolving disputes, assist in doing a good job in community correction and helping persons released after serving their sentences, and assist in doing a good job in responding to emergencies.
The villagers committee shall support and guide social organizations, social workers, volunteers, and other social forces to participate in rural governance and services.
In a village inhabited by multiple ethnic groups, the villagers committee shall support and guide villagers of all ethnic groups to enhance unity, respect each other, and help each other.

The villagers committee and its members shall abide by the Constitution, laws, and regulations, abide by the policies of the Party and the State, abide by and organize the implementation of the villagers' self-governance charter and village rules and conventions, implement the decisions and resolutions of the villagers assembly and the villagers representative assembly, act fairly, be honest in performing their duties, be enthusiastic in serving the villagers, and accept the supervision of the villagers.

A villagers committee shall have the legal person status of a primary-level mass self-governance organization, and the director of the villagers committee shall be the legal representative. The villagers committee may engage in civil activities necessary for the performance of its functions, but shall not provide guarantees.

The director, deputy directors, and members of the villagers committee shall be directly elected by the villagers. No organization or individual shall designate, appoint, or remove members of the villagers committee.
The villagers committee shall have a term of five years, and a re-election shall be held in a timely manner upon the expiration of the term. Members of the villagers committee may be re-elected.

The election of a villagers committee shall be presided over by a villagers electoral committee.
The villagers electoral committee shall be composed of a director, deputy directors, and members, and shall be elected by the villagers assembly, the villagers representative assembly, or the meetings of each villagers group.
Where a member of the villagers electoral committee or his or her close relative is nominated as a candidate for membership of the villagers committee, the member shall withdraw from the villagers electoral committee.
Where a member of the villagers electoral committee withdraws from the villagers electoral committee or becomes vacant due to other reasons, a replacement shall be made in order according to the original election results, or a new election may be held.

The list of villagers registered to participate in the election shall be published by the villagers electoral committee twenty days before the election day.
Any person who has an objection to the list of villagers registered to participate in the election shall file a petition with the villagers electoral committee within five days from the date of publication of the list, and the villagers electoral committee shall make a decision on the handling within three days from the date of receipt of the petition and publish the handling result.

Candidates for members of the villagers committee shall be nominated and recommended by the village Party organization or by villagers registered to participate in the election. When nominating and recommending candidates, the interests of all villagers shall be taken as the starting point, and villagers who support the leadership of the Communist Party of China, abide by the law, have good conduct, are fair and upright, are enthusiastic about public welfare, and have a certain level of education and work ability shall be recommended as candidates. Persons who have been expelled from the Communist Party of China, have been subject to criminal punishment for crimes, have used clan or black and evil forces to engage in illegal activities, or have organized or participated in illegal religious activities or cult activities shall not serve as candidates. The number of candidates shall be greater than the number of persons to be elected. The villagers electoral committee shall organize meetings between candidates and villagers, at which candidates shall introduce their visions for fulfilling their duties and answer questions raised by villagers.
In the election of a villagers committee, the election shall be valid if more than half of the villagers registered to participate in the election cast their votes; a candidate shall be elected only if he or she receives more than half of the votes cast by the villagers who participate in the voting. If the number of persons elected is less than the number to be elected, a supplementary election shall be held for the shortfall. In the supplementary election, the persons who have received the most votes among those who were not elected in the first round of voting shall be the candidates, and the candidates shall be elected on the basis of receiving the most votes, provided that the number of votes received shall not be less than one-third of the total number of votes cast.
The election shall be conducted by secret ballot and open counting of votes, and the election results shall be announced on the spot. During the election, a secret ballot booth shall be set up.
Villagers registered to participate in the election who are unable to vote due to being away during the election period may entrust in writing a close relative who has the right to vote in the village or another villager to vote on their behalf. No villager may accept entrustment from more than three persons. Candidates shall not accept entrustment to vote. The villagers electoral committee shall publish the list of the principals and the entrusted persons.
The specific election procedures shall be prescribed by the standing committee of the people's congress of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

A request to recall a member of the villagers committee may be made jointly by more than one-fifth of the villagers with the right to vote in the village or more than one-third of the villagers' representatives, stating the reasons for the recall. The member of the villagers committee who is subject to the recall shall have the right to present a defense.
To recall a member of the villagers committee, more than half of the villagers registered to participate in the election shall cast their votes, and the recall shall be approved by more than half of the villagers who have voted.

A member of the villagers committee may submit a resignation application to the villagers committee, and his or her position shall terminate from the date on which the resignation is considered and approved by the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly.

Any person who is elected as a member of the villagers committee by improper means such as violence, threats, deception, bribery, forging ballots, or falsely reporting the number of votes cast shall have his or her election declared invalid.
With respect to acts that interfere with villagers' exercise of the right to vote and stand for election and undermine the election of the villagers committee by improper means such as violence, threats, deception, bribery, forging ballots, or falsely reporting the number of votes cast, villagers shall have the right to report to the people's congress and the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town, or to the standing committee of the people's congress at the county level and the people's government at the county level and their relevant competent departments. The people's government at the township level or the county level shall be responsible for investigating and handling the matter according to law.
Where a member of the villagers committee loses capacity for civil conduct or is sentenced to criminal punishment, his or her position shall be automatically terminated.

Where a vacancy arises among the members of the villagers committee, a by-election may be conducted by the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly. The procedures for the by-election shall be carried out by reference to the provisions of Article 18 of this Law. The term of office of a member elected in the by-election shall end upon the expiration of the term of office of the current villagers committee.

The villagers committee shall complete the handover of work within ten days from the date on which the new term of the villagers committee is formed. The handover of work shall be presided over by the villagers electoral committee and supervised by the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town.

The villagers assembly shall be composed of villagers who have reached the age of 18 in the village.
The villagers assembly shall be convened by the villagers committee. Where more than one-tenth of the villagers or more than one-third of the villagers' representatives propose, the villagers assembly shall be convened. When convening the villagers assembly, the villagers shall be notified ten days in advance; in special circumstances, the villagers may be notified on an ad hoc basis.
The villagers assembly shall be held at least once a year.

To convene a villagers assembly, more than half of the villagers in the village who have reached the age of 18, or representatives of more than two-thirds of the households in the village, shall be present; decisions made by the villagers assembly shall be approved by more than half of the persons present. Where laws provide otherwise for convening the villagers assembly and making decisions, those provisions shall prevail.
When convening the villagers assembly, representatives of enterprises, public institutions, and mass organizations located in the village may be invited to attend as non-voting participants as needed.

The villagers assembly shall review the annual work report of the villagers committee and appraise the work of the members of the villagers committee; it shall have the power to annul or modify inappropriate decisions of the villagers committee; it shall have the power to annul or modify inappropriate decisions of the villagers representative assembly.
The villagers assembly may authorize the villagers representative assembly to review the annual work report of the villagers committee, appraise the work of the members of the villagers committee, and annul or modify inappropriate decisions of the villagers committee.

In a village with a relatively large population or scattered residences, a villagers representative assembly may be established to discuss and decide matters authorized by the villagers assembly. The villagers representative assembly shall be composed of members of the villagers committee and villagers' representatives. Villagers' representatives shall account for no less than four-fifths of the members of the villagers representative assembly, and female villagers' representatives shall account for no less than one-third of the members of the villagers representative assembly.
Villagers' representatives shall be elected by the villagers on the basis of one representative for every five to fifteen households, or by each villagers group to elect a certain number of representatives. The term of office of villagers' representatives shall be the same as that of the villagers committee. Villagers' representatives may be re-elected.
Villagers' representatives shall be responsible to the households or villagers group that elected them and shall accept the supervision of the villagers.

The villagers representative assembly shall be convened by the villagers committee. The villagers representative assembly shall be held once every quarter. Where more than one-fifth of the villagers' representatives propose, the villagers representative assembly shall be convened.
The villagers representative assembly may be held only if more than two-thirds of its members are present, and decisions made shall be approved by more than half of the persons present.

The villagers assembly may formulate and amend the villagers' self-governance charter and village rules and conventions, and shall report them to the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town for recordation.
The villagers' self-governance charter, village rules and conventions, and decisions of the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly shall not contravene the Constitution, laws, or regulations, shall not violate public order and good customs, and shall not contain content that infringes upon the personal rights, democratic rights, and property rights of villagers.
Where the villagers' self-governance charter, village rules and conventions, or decisions of the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly violate the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town shall order correction.

A villagers group shall carry out activities under the organization of the villagers committee. A villagers group meeting shall discuss and decide important matters of the villagers group.
To convene a villagers group meeting, more than two-thirds of the villagers in the group who have reached the age of 18, or representatives of more than two-thirds of the households in the group, shall be present, and decisions made shall be approved by more than half of the persons present.
The head of a villagers group shall be elected by the villagers group meeting. The term of office of the head of a villagers group shall be the same as that of the villagers committee, and he or she may be re-elected.
Where a villagers group exercises the functions of a rural collective economic organization, the villagers group meeting shall, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, discuss and decide on the management of land, enterprises, and other property collectively owned by the villagers group, as well as the handling of public welfare matters. The decisions made and the implementation situation shall be promptly published to the villagers of the group.

With respect to public affairs, public welfare undertakings that involve the vital interests of villagers, as well as actual difficulties and disputes reflected by villagers, the villagers committee shall organize villagers and other stakeholders to conduct consultations.
Consultations may take various forms such as council meetings, hearings, and symposiums, and, as needed, relevant departments of the people's government, the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town, mass organizations, deputies to the people's congress, and members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference may be invited to participate. Matters involving a high level of expertise such as agricultural science and technology and engineering construction may be addressed by inviting relevant professionals to participate.
With respect to matters determined through consultation, the villagers committee shall organize implementation or supervise implementation in a timely manner; where the matter needs to be submitted to the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly, a meeting shall be convened to discuss and decide.

The villagers committee shall practice a democratic decision-making mechanism of the minority being subordinate to the majority and the work principle of openness and transparency, and shall establish and improve various work systems.

Where the villagers committee fails to publish in a timely manner matters that should be published or publishes matters that are untrue, villagers shall have the right to report to the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town, or to the people's government at the county level and its relevant competent departments. The relevant people's government or competent department shall be responsible for investigating and verifying the matter and ordering publication according to law; if there is indeed any illegal act after verification, the relevant persons shall bear liability according to law.

A village shall establish a village affairs supervision committee or other forms of village affairs supervision bodies, which shall be responsible for villagers' democratic financial management and for supervising the implementation of systems such as openness of village affairs. Its members shall be elected by the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly from among the villagers, and there shall be persons with knowledge of finance, accounting, and management. The members of the villagers committee and their close relatives shall not serve as members of the village affairs supervision body. The term of office of the village affairs supervision body shall be the same as that of the villagers committee.
The village affairs supervision body shall be responsible to the villagers assembly and the villagers representative assembly, and its members may attend meetings of the villagers committee and the villagers representative assembly as non-voting participants and participate in various consultation activities.
Where, in the course of performing its duties, the village affairs supervision body discovers any violation of discipline or law that infringes upon the interests of the masses, it shall report to the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town, or to the people's government at the county level and the supervisory organ.

Members of the villagers committee and hired personnel whose work-failure subsidies are borne by the villagers or the village collective shall accept democratic appraisal by the villagers assembly or the villagers representative assembly of their performance of duties. Democratic appraisal shall be conducted at least once a year, and shall be presided over by the village affairs supervision body.
Where a member of the villagers committee is appraised as incompetent for two consecutive times, his or her position shall be terminated.

The villagers committee and the village affairs supervision body shall establish village affairs archives. Village affairs archives shall include: election documents and ballots, meeting minutes, basic data of public welfare facilities, basic construction data, etc. The village affairs archives shall be authentic, accurate, complete, and standardized.

Where a decision made by the villagers committee or a member of the villagers committee infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of a villager, the aggrieved villager may apply to the People's Court for annulment, and the responsible person shall bear legal liability according to law.
Where the villagers committee fails to perform its legal obligations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations, the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town shall order correction.
Where the people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town interferes with matters that fall within the scope of villagers' self-governance according to law, the people's government at the next higher level shall order correction.

The standards for daily operation funds of the villagers committee and the basic remuneration of its members shall be prescribed by the people's government at or above the county level, and the people's government at the county level shall provide appropriate subsidies.
The funds required for the villagers committee to handle public welfare undertakings in the village shall be raised through fund-raising and labor contribution by the villagers assembly; where there is genuine difficulty in funds, the local people's government shall provide appropriate support.
The income of the village collective economy shall be appropriately used for village public affairs and public welfare undertakings, the guarantee of the operation of the villagers committee, and subsidies for persons who miss work.

The people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town shall provide necessary funds and conditions for the villagers committee to assist the government in carrying out its work.
Local people's governments at all levels shall establish and improve a long-term mechanism for combating formalism and reducing burdens at the grassroots level. Matters on which relevant departments entrust the villagers committee to assist in carrying out work shall comply with the provisions of laws and regulations, and the necessary funds shall be borne by the entrusting department.

The construction of comprehensive service facilities at the village level shall be included in relevant plans. Local people's governments at or above the county level shall provide support for the construction of comprehensive service facilities at the village level.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall make overall plans and implementation for the informatization construction of rural governance, and encourage and support the villagers committee to use modern information technology to serve the villagers.

The people's government of a township, ethnic township, or town or the people's government at the county level shall provide training for the members of the villagers committee and other village affairs workers, helping them to improve their political quality, awareness of the rule of law, policy level, and service capacity.

Where a city not divided into districts, a municipal district, a subdistrict, or a development zone, forest area, or reclamation area establishes a villagers committee, the relevant provisions of this Law shall apply.

State organs, organizations, military units, state-owned and state-controlled enterprises, public institutions, and their personnel stationed in rural areas shall not participate in the organization of the villagers committee, but shall participate in rural construction through various forms and abide by the relevant village rules and conventions.
Where the villagers committee, the villagers assembly, or the villagers representative assembly discusses and decides matters related to the units specified in the preceding paragraph, they shall consult with such units.

Local people's congresses at all levels and the standing committees of local people's congresses at or above the county level shall ensure the implementation of this Law within their respective administrative regions and guarantee that villagers exercise their self-governance rights according to law.

The standing committees of the people's congresses of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in accordance with this Law and in light of the actual circumstances of their respective administrative regions, formulate implementing measures.
This Law shall come into force as of the date of its promulgation.
